- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show strong mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes; model tends to overreact and peak too high, then fails to correct.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 10–20 day window, especially when historical mean is rising.
- When true values show strong downward momentum after a spike, model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model underestimates when true values are trending downward from a recent peak, especially in the 20–30 day window.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility, leading to overestimation of short-term price movements.
- When historical mean is stable or declining, model often overestimates the mean, leading to persistent overprediction.
- Model underestimates when true values are near or below historical mean, especially in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model shows lag in correcting for downward trends, often underestimating the depth of correction.
